technique: Full 3D CG animation with a caricatured character rig (elongated triangular noses, oversized white-sclera eyes, simplified peg-like hands and feet) rendered with a fuzzed felt/wool-fiber cloth shader on the woman's sweater that visually nods to stop-motion/claymation without actually being physical puppetry. Evidence against true stop-motion: the running crowd (periodic-1/2) shows continuous motion blur on legs and hair rather than frame-holds, and the background tsunami wave is a smoothly lit, photoreal-ish fluid simulation with soft foam detail that would be extremely costly to achieve as a practical set. This is a repost/compilation account ("Low Battery People," title card credits "Nin.") showing a clip from a separately produced CG short, with an added text title card and burned-in dialogue captions ("KISSING", "PART?", "KNOW") rather than any animation made by the reposting channel itself.
facial_animation_notes: Faces use a small number of clearly distinct blend-shape poses rather than continuous micro-expression drift: across periodic-4 through periodic-13 the same two characters snap between a wide-eyed/eyebrows-raised 'shocked' pose (periodic-4,5,6,7,8,13) and a half-lidded, brow-lowered 'unimpressed/deadpan' pose (periodic-9,10,11,12) with almost no intermediate states visible in the sampled frames, giving a punchy, pose-to-pose comedic rhythm typical of keyframed CG dialogue animation. Mouths open into simple rounded 'scream' shapes during the running scene (periodic-1,2,3) and into smaller talking shapes during the dialogue (periodic-7,8), with visible teeth only in the angriest pose (periodic-12).
eye_and_blink_notes: No mid-blink frame is caught in the sample, but eyelid position is doing heavy comedic lifting: fully open white ovals with visible pupils signal panic/surprise (periodic-4 through -8, -13), while the same character's eyes narrow to sagging half-lidded slits in periodic-9 through -12 to sell exasperation/sarcasm mid-apocalypse. Eyes stay locked on each other in the two-shot rather than glancing away, reinforcing a static 'face-off' staging.
head_movement_notes: In the crowd-run frames (periodic-1,2,3) heads bob and turn individually per running figure, each on its own phase, giving the crowd an asynchronous, non-cloned feel. In the two-character dialogue block, head movement is minimal and confined to small tilts/tucks -- the man's head cranes slightly forward and down toward the woman in periodic-9/10, and both heads pivot a few degrees toward each other -- while the wave background stays essentially locked in place behind them across ten consecutive periodic samples, suggesting a mostly static two-shot with the animation load carried by the faces and hands rather than the camera or head rig.
gesture_notes: Both characters keep clasped, wringing hand gestures in front of the torso through the dialogue scene (periodic-4 through -8), with finger positions shifting slightly frame to frame (e.g., the man's hand opens from a loose fist in periodic-3 to splayed fingers in periodic-5) -- a small, nervous, contained gesture vocabulary rather than broad arm swings. During the running scene, arms pump and swing widely and asynchronously across the crowd (periodic-1,2), contrasting with the tight, restrained hand acting once the scene cuts to the two-shot.
idle_motion_notes: Loose strands of hair escaping the woman's bun visibly change angle/position between periodic-9 and periodic-10, implying a light secondary hair-sim or wind sway even though her head is nearly still. Scattered debris (papers, cans, shoes) on the road is static across frames rather than blowing, and the giant wave itself barely changes shape across ~10 sampled frames -- read together, this looks like a deliberate 'frozen moment' staging device (the world paused mid-catastrophe for the joke) rather than an animation limitation.
frame_rate_feel: Source is 30fps per metadata.json. The crowd-running frames show smooth motion blur on legs and papers consistent with full-rate or near-full-rate animation rather than 2s/3s stepped holds. The dialogue portion reads as choppier only because of large pose-to-pose jumps in eyebrow/eyelid state between the sparsely-sampled periodic frames (~1s apart) -- within any single expression the surfaces (cloth fuzz, hair) look continuously rendered, so the apparent 'snap' is a keyframed acting choice, not a low-frame-rate artifact.
overall_animation_style_notes: The clip pairs broad, silent-movie-style pantomime (screaming crowd, exaggerated running) with a tightly-held two-shot built on subtle eye/eyebrow acting and small hand gestures for the comedic 'mundane conversation during the apocalypse' beat. The felt-textured cloth shader and long-nosed, big-eyed character design give a handcrafted/stop-motion flavor, but the fluid wave simulation and blur-smooth crowd motion point to digital 3D CG rather than physical puppets. Text overlays (title card, episode number, burned-in captions) are added by the reposting 'Low Battery People' account and are not part of the underlying character animation.
